teaser_types._note: The teaser is the first thing the reader sees — before the headline, before any prose. It must create curiosity on its own. Choose ONE. Generate the asset if it is an image or video; save to PROJECT_DIR/assets/teaser.*.
teaser_types.interactive_experience: The core finding can be felt before being explained. Reader participates, then sees the data. Highest engagement — use whenever the topic allows.
teaser_types.video: Motion, transformation, or atmosphere that a still image can't convey.
teaser_types.generated_image: Strong emotional or cinematic visual. Full-bleed, no text.

per_section_modes._note: For every edt_xx section, decide the presentation. Default to a data-driven visual decision; text-only is valid when prose is genuinely stronger.
per_section_modes.interactive_chart: Reader benefits from exploring, filtering, or comparing (e.g. by demographic, time, group).
per_section_modes.static_chart: A decisive single comparison; no exploration needed.
per_section_modes.interactive_map: Data has a geographic dimension. Use Leaflet.js (CDN ok) with markers, choropleth, or animated paths. Strongly prefer whenever the data has lat/lng, city names, country codes, or station locations.
per_section_modes.interactive_timeline: Data spans time — events, eras, changes over years. A scrollable timeline readers can scrub. If there are many labeled stops, prefer a responsive numbered-card stack that still reads cleanly inside the story column.
per_section_modes.scrollytelling: The narrative builds step by step — each scroll step triggers a visual change (map zoom, chart filter, new layer). Implement with IntersectionObserver + CSS transitions.
per_section_modes.before_after_slider: Two states need direct comparison — drag a slider to reveal the difference. Works for maps, charts (two periods), or images.
per_section_modes.card_deck_swipe: Many comparable items the reader wants to browse one by one — swipeable cards (artworks, wines, players, cases) with key info + image if available.
per_section_modes.reader_quiz_guess_first: The finding is surprising — let the reader guess before revealing. Maximizes the surprise factor.
per_section_modes.interactive_demo_minigame: The finding is experiential — reader should discover it, not just read it.
per_section_modes.generated_image: Emotional beat, analogy, or scene that data cannot show.
per_section_modes.event_reenactment_video: The section describes a specific event, incident, or anecdote — generate a short video that shows what happened. Strongly prefer over a static image whenever the prose describes something that happened.
per_section_modes.image_to_video: You already have a strong generated image for this section — animate it with subtle motion to make it feel alive.
per_section_modes.stat_callout: One big number that speaks for itself.
per_section_modes.audio_music: The topic involves music, sound, rhythm, speech, ambience, or data that can be meaningfully heard. Always pair with a visual fallback.
per_section_modes.text_only: Rare — only when prose alone is the whole point.

science_paper_modes._note: Available when the blog is about a scientific paper.
science_paper_modes.pdf_page_preview: Show a specific page/region of the paper via PDF.js with zoom and navigation. Great for the key figure, abstract, or a controversial table.
science_paper_modes.paper_anatomy_diagram: Interactive breakdown of the paper's structure — click sections to see proportion, reviewer comments, key content. A visual X-ray.
science_paper_modes.review_scorecard: Radar or grouped bar chart of reviewer scores across dimensions (novelty, clarity, significance, soundness). When reviewers disagree, the tension is immediate.
science_paper_modes.review_disagreement_heatmap: Matrix showing which aspects each reviewer scored differently. Highlights where the 'war' happened.
science_paper_modes.concern_taxonomy_treemap: Treemap or sunburst of reviewer concerns by category (novelty, experiments, writing, theory). Size = frequency or severity.
science_paper_modes.citation_network: Force-directed graph (D3.js) showing the paper's position relative to references and citers. Node size = citation count, edges = citation relationships, click to see titles.
science_paper_modes.experiment_comparison_table: Interactive sortable/filterable table comparing methods across datasets. Highlight winning cells.
science_paper_modes.figure_reproduction_enhancement: Take the paper's original figure and either reproduce it with better styling or present original vs enhanced in a before/after slider.
science_paper_modes.timeline_of_discovery: Horizontal timeline of the paper's lineage — prior works, this paper's contribution, subsequent work that built on it.
science_paper_modes.paper_review_browser: Accordion or tab panel showing individual papers with review details (scores, comments, audit reports). Each expandable with title, scores (AI/human), verdict badge, key findings, quotes, external link. Use when the dataset has multiple papers with review/audit metadata. Pair with a Notable Papers card section for a browse → deep-dive flow.
science_paper_modes.task_demo: Interactive tabbed panel showing a concrete input→output example of the paper's method. Tabs: Input (raw data), Reasoning/Process (intermediate steps, chain-of-thought), Output (final result with annotations). Use whenever the paper describes a system/model/pipeline. Detective or Analyst should extract a representative example. Spec which example to show, what to highlight, and color-coding for data types. Strongly prefer for any ML/AI/computational paper.

video_encouragement: When the editor's prose describes a concrete event, incident, or anecdote (e.g. 'a lawyer submitted a brief with fabricated citations'), strongly consider generating a short video to SHOW that moment. A 5-second clip is far more engaging than a static image. Use text2video for full scenes, or image2video to animate a generated still.
what_to_write_per_section: Rationale: why this mode, not another
Spec: precise description of what the visual shows, what interaction does, what data is used, what the reader experiences
Asset file: filename in PROJECT_DIR/assets/ (if generated)
chart_spec_requirements: Do not generate chart code — write a precise spec the Programmer implements: chart type; which ana_xx data_table provides the data (data_source); X/Y/color encoding (use column names from the data_table); for facet/small-multiple/concat compositions specify column count, per-panel width, spacing; what to highlight; interaction behavior; style notes.
interactive_spec_requirements: Write a step-by-step interaction spec: initial state (what the reader sees) → trigger (click/type/drag) → transition (what changes and how) → payoff (what is revealed and how it connects to the finding).
